english.title: Aid / abet a person to threaten another with an offensive weapon in a public place

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Legal Aid Sentencing and punishment of offenders Act 2012

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) had with

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

an offensive weapon, namely **(..SPECIFY THE WEAPON..), in a public place, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), and you aided, abetted, counselled or procured,

(C)_[him]_
(D)_[her]_

to unlawfully and intentionally threaten another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON THREATENED..), with that weapon in such a way that there was an immediate risk of serious physical harm to that other person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1A of the Prevention of Crime Act 1953 and section 8 of the Accessories and Abettors Act 1861.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 1A(2) of the Prevention of Crime Act 1953 for meaning of serious physical harm - amounts to grievous bodily harm for the purposes of the Offences Against the Person Act 1861.
(ii) See section 1A(5) of the Prevention of Crime Act 1953 for the circumstances where the court must impose a custodial sentence.
(iii) See section 1(4) of the Prevention of Crime Act 1953 for meaning of "public place" and "offensive weapon".
(iv) The court may find the defendant not guilty of this offence but guilty of an offence under section 1 of the Act.
(v) The Offensive Weapons Act 2019 amended the offence to include an objective element - whether a reasonable person exposed to the threat would think there was an immediate risk of physical harm. For offences committed on or after 6th April 2022 see H20301.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 4 years imprisonment and / or a fine.
For minimum sentence for this offence see section 312 of the Sentencing Act 2020.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
